turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, Oksana, come on in. Before anything else, can you give me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oksana Kovalenko, August 30th, 1979.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you. How's the Soryasi's been?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Honestly, worse. Over the last four months, it's spread. My elbows and knees are bad again, there's a big patch on my lower back, and my scalp itches like crazy. I've had this for eight years, and this is the worst it's been.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm sorry. Are you still using the clopetosol ointment?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, twice a day on the worst spots. It helps for a few days, and then it all comes back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And the methotrexate from last spring?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I stopped that on my own in June. I was on 10 milligrams a week. No, wait, it was 15, 6 of the little 2 .5 pills. It made me so nauseous and my hair got thin.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful. Thank you for telling me. Let me ask about your joints. Any joint pain or swelling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Stiffness in the morning. Sausage -like swelling of a finger or toe. Heal pain.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that. My mom had rheumatoid arthritis in her hands, so I'd notice, believe me.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good. Other medicines.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Amlodipine, five milligrams every morning for blood pressure.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's it. And you're allergic to Sulfa, right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, I get a rash all over.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Still not smoking.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Three years quit now.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's great.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: let me look. On both elbows, there are well -defined red plaques with thick silvery scale. The right one is about 8 x 6 cm. Similar plaques on both knees. On the lower back, there's a 10 x 7 cm plaque. on the scalp. Red scaly plaques behind both ears and along the hairline. I see pitting on three of your fingernails. Your finger joints aren't swollen or tender and no swollen fingers or toes. Overall about 12 % of your body surface.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 12 %? That sounds like a lot.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It is. So this is moderate to severe plaque psoriasis that isn't controlled with creams, and methotrexate didn't work out for you. I think you're a really good candidate for a biologic. The one I'd recommend is Risinkizumab. It's an injection under the skin, 150 milligrams, given at week zero, week four, just every 12 weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every 12 weeks? That's not bad.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: What are the risks? It calms down part of the immune system, so there's a slightly higher chance of infections, like colds. Serious problems are rare. Before we start, I need a TB blood test, hepatitis B and C tests, a blood count, and a metabolic panel. You should also avoid live vaccines once you're on it, so getting your flu shot this fall is a good idea.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, can I do the blood work at the lab by my house? It's at 2250 Riverside Drive.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll send the orders there. We'll also need a prior authorization from your insurance. Do you have your card?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, member ID is K as in kilo 7 0 3 9 2 1 5.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it. In the meantime, keep the Clopetosol ointment twice a day on the body plaques, but only two weeks at a time, then a week off, so the skin doesn't thin. For your scalp, I'm adding Clopetosol 0 .05 % solution, once a day at night.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, my husband Taras will be thrilled. He's tired of the flakes on the couch. Huh,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: and if you ever do get joint pain, swelling, or morning stiffness, tell me right away, because psoriasis can affect the joints and that changes treatment. Best number to reach you with lab results.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great. Once the labs and insurance approval come back, we'll have you in for the first injection and teach you how to do it. Otherwise, follow up in six weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you, Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Nair.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm actually hopeful.
